therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: Diabetic patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in post-bronchodilator FEV1 and DLco over 52 weeks

results.effect_size: FEV1 change at Week 52: Inhaled Insulin -0.068 L vs Subcutaneous Insulin -0.128 L; DLco change at Week 52: Inhaled Insulin -0.614 mL/min/mmHg vs Subcutaneous Insulin -0.882 mL/min/mmHg
results.target_engagement_evidence: Fasting plasma glucose reductions observed in inhaled insulin arm (e.g., -23.40 mg/dL at Week 52 vs +12.37 mg/dL for subcutaneous)
biomarker_changes: HbA1c change at Week 52 LOCF: Inhaled Insulin -0.28% vs Subcutaneous Insulin -0.26%
Fasting plasma glucose change at Week 52 LOCF: Inhaled Insulin -28.55 mg/dL vs Subcutaneous Insulin +2.36 mg/dL
Body weight change at Week 52 LOCF: Inhaled Insulin +0.99 kg vs Subcutaneous Insulin +2.40 kg
subgroup_findings: FEV1 decline appeared numerically smaller in inhaled insulin arm vs subcutaneous at most timepoints
DLco decline appeared numerically smaller in inhaled insulin arm at Week 52 (-0.614 vs -0.882 mL/min/mmHg)
Hypoglycemic event rates overall similar: Inhaled Insulin 0.89 vs Subcutaneous Insulin 0.84 events/subject-month
Severe hypoglycemic event rates overall: Inhaled Insulin 0.64 vs Subcutaneous Insulin 0.22 events/100 subject-months
safety_signals: Severe hypoglycemic event rate numerically higher in inhaled insulin arm (0.64 vs 0.22 events/100 subject-months overall)
Myocardial infarction: 1/59 inhaled insulin vs 3/46 subcutaneous insulin
Coronary artery disease: 0/59 inhaled insulin vs 2/46 subcutaneous insulin

dose_info.dose: Adjusted according to premeal blood glucose
dose_info.dose_modifications: Dose adjusted according to premeal blood glucose throughout study

context.indication: Diabetes mellitus with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)
context.investigator_commentary: Trial was terminated; termination reason referenced in detailed description but not fully specified in available record. Trial enrolled diabetic patients with COPD to assess pulmonary safety (FEV1, DLco) and glycemic efficacy of inhaled insulin versus subcutaneous insulin over one year.
